status: REJECTED_AS_TRADING_STRATEGY (2026-09-15, post-characterization) -- see amendment below. Forward paper test in FORWARD_PROTOCOL.md is cancelled, not launched.
rejection_amendment: The full pre-execution veto (candidates removed before execute_cluster, so removing one candidate can free the single global position slot for a different one) produced a materially weaker result than S45c's per-trade diagnostic coefficient (-0.593R, p=0.002) implied: combined across all three historical windows, 231 trades, net +$1.79 at base costs (+$0.0045/day on $250, ~5500x short of the $25/day target) and -$20.15 at stress costs (net losing). This gap between the diagnostic effect and the full-system result is itself informative: filtering 'bad' realized trades out of a fixed historical list does not account for how removing a candidate changes which OTHER candidate wins the shared position slot, equity path, and daily-stop state -- exactly the mechanism this protocol's own execution section warned about, now empirically confirmed to matter. A naive 5x->30x leverage multiplier (6x) on the base result would still only reach ~$0.027/day, nowhere near $25/day, and would scale the stress-cost loss by the same factor -- leverage cannot bridge a ~5500x gap. Verdict: funding remains an interesting research signal (the diagnostic coefficient was real and well-controlled) but did not translate into a working trading system at this capital/frequency. S46 is closed. No S47 in this same order-block+OI lineage is planned; the next research direction changes the underlying edge source instead of further filtering this one.
motivating_context: S45/S45b/S45c diagnosed S20 H1's already-realized trades (no new entry logic tested there) for a stable, symbol-and-side-controlled negative-funding effect. S45c's frozen decision rule (agreed BEFORE reading its output): P(beta<0)>=95% in a bootstrap of the negative_funding coefficient from r_multiple ~ negative_funding + C(symbol) + C(window) + C(side) (HC3 robust OLS), AND leave-one-symbol-out not causing the effect to vanish, => S46 GO. Result: HC3 coefficient -0.593R (p=0.002, 95% CI [-0.961,-0.225]); bootstrap median -0.592R, 95% CI [-0.978,-0.241], P(beta<0)=99.97%; leave-one-out without SOLUSDT still shows the effect in validation and retrospective_evaluation (only development flips sign), judged 'does not vanish' per the frozen rule. GO was called. S46 is the resulting single-rule strategy.
critical_status_disclosure: S46 is a FROZEN FORWARD CANDIDATE, not a validated or promotable strategy. The funding<0 veto was discovered by examining these exact development/validation/retrospective_evaluation windows -- any backtest of S46 on those same windows is IN-SAMPLE / DISCOVERY-AFFECTED and must never be reported or referred to as 'validation'. The historical backtest below exists purely for characterization (trade count, drawdown shape, symbol/side mix, monthly PnL, losing-streak length) -- it is not a gate and does not by itself justify any promotion. The only legitimate gate for this rule is genuinely new data collected strictly after this protocol was frozen (forward paper trading).
rule: Exactly one addition to S20 H1, evaluated at each candidate's own signal timestamp, strictly before execution: look up the most recently known funding rate for that symbol using timestamps STRICTLY BEFORE the signal timestamp (never at or after); if no such rate exists, or it is negative, reject the candidate. All other S20 H1 logic (order block, 4h/1h regime, OBV, OI confirmation using S20's original unfixed sign convention, breakeven+chandelier exit: partial 1.5R, trail 2.5x ATR, cap 8R) is unchanged.
no_tuning_disclosure: No magnitude threshold on the funding rate (e.g. -0.001%, -0.003%) was or will be swept -- the binary funding<0 veto is frozen exactly as discovered. No funding moving average, momentum, symbol-specific threshold, combination with S44A's OI fix, S44C's liquidity filter, or the S45 BTC regime filter, and no leverage/sizing change. Tuning any of these now would destroy the property that made this candidate different from every other rejected route in this project: it was frozen before being seen on new data, not iterated until it looked good.

symbols.note: Identical to S20 -- reuses the exact same cached klines/funding/metrics archives, no new data source.

windows.genuine_oos: new data after this protocol's freeze timestamp -- the only legitimate gate for this specific rule; frozen 2026-09-15

characterization_only_metrics: trades, wins, PF base, PF stress

execution.one_global_position: single global minute event loop with one shared cash balance, pending order and open position across the correlated ETH/SOL/BNB cluster -- the funding veto is applied to candidates BEFORE they enter this arbitration, not filtered from an already-realized trade list, since removing a candidate can free a slot for a different one

sensitivity_audit_deferred: The S45c bootstrap resampled individual trades as independent draws; crypto trades can be time-correlated, and a block/cluster bootstrap by week or month would likely widen the CI. This is deferred to a later sensitivity audit and explicitly does NOT reopen the GO decision -- the decision rule was frozen before the result was seen, and the bar is not moved after the fact because a stricter check might narrow the margin.
known_limitations: IN-SAMPLE / DISCOVERY-AFFECTED historical backtest -- see critical_status_disclosure. Do not treat as validation under any framing.
The funding veto meaningfully reduces the candidate pool (removing ~25-35% of prior S20 H1 candidates per window); this is expected and was disclosed before this protocol was written.
If forward paper trading shows the effect does not hold, this rule is abandoned outright -- it does not get a magnitude threshold added post-hoc to 'save' it.
No leverage or position-sizing change is bundled with this protocol; that is explicitly deferred until (and only if) forward data confirms the edge.
